You have an SAP production landscape in Azure in the North Europe Azure region.  
  
You need to recommend a disaster-recovery solution that ensures services remain available in the West Europe Azure region if the North Europe region is unavailable. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Support the minimum recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO).  
- Support a two-node SAP Central Services (SCS) cluster.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should the recommendation include?
questions.explanation:
Azure Site Recovery replicates Azure virtual machines to a secondary Azure region and supports disaster-recovery failover plans for SAP workloads. Microsoft’s SAP guidance recommends it for SAP Central Services, including highly available cluster configurations, with required cluster reconfiguration and supporting resources in the DR region after failover. It is designed to meet defined RTO and RPO requirements while avoiding the cost of operating a fully active duplicate landscape.

**Learn more:** [Disaster Recovery recommendation for SAP workload](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/disaster-recovery-sap-guide) · [Set up SAP NetWeaver disaster recovery with Azure Site Recovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/site-recovery/site-recovery-sap)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to deploy a production SAP landscape on Azure.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that minimizes latency between the application servers and the SAP HANA database server.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: Deploy the virtual machines to a proximity placement group.
Route all traffic between the virtual machines through an Azure Standard Load Balancer.
Route all traffic between the virtual machines through load-balanced network virtual appliances (NVAs).
Deploy the virtual machines to the same subnet.

questions.explanation:
Azure proximity placement groups apply a physical colocation constraint to compute resources, placing the SAP application-server and SAP HANA database VMs close together for the lowest possible network latency. SAP application and database tiers are particularly sensitive to network round-trip time because of their frequent communication.

**Learn more:** [Configuration options to minimize network latency with SAP applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/proximity-placement-scenarios) · [Proximity placement groups - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/co-location)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises SAP AnyDB deployment running on an operating system that is **not** supported in Azure.  
  
You need to migrate the deployment to Azure by replatforming it and migrating to SAP HANA. The solution must meet these requirements:

- Minimize downtime.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
SAP Software Update Manager (SUM), with its Database Migration Option (DMO), performs the SAP workload upgrade/replatforming and migration from AnyDB to SAP HANA in one process. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two Azure subscriptions.  
  
You plan to deploy virtual machines in both subscriptions. The virtual machines will host SAP workloads. As part of the deployment, the virtual machines will be placed in an availability zone named Availability Zone 1 in each subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that the virtual machines reside in the same physical datacenter.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Use the Check Zone Peers REST API.
Deploy the virtual machines to the same availability set.
Deploy the virtual machines to the same proximity group.
Use the List By Location REST API.

questions.explanation:
Availability-zone identifiers are logical mappings that can differ between Azure subscriptions, so Availability Zone 1 is not necessarily the same physical datacenter in both subscriptions. The Check Zone Peers API compares the subscriptions’ logical zone mappings and returns the corresponding physical-zone peers needed to select matching zones.

**Learn more:** [Subscriptions - Check Zone Peers - REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/resources/subscriptions/check-zone-peers?view=rest-resources-2022-12-01) · [What are Azure availability zones?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/availability-zones-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an existing SAP production landscape in Azure. The SAP application virtual machines use static IP addresses.  
  
You need to replicate the virtual machines to a different Azure region by using Azure Site Recovery. The source and target subnets use different address ranges.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

Azure Site Recovery must replicate the virtual machines, and target network settings must be modified to assign suitable addresses in the target subnet because a different address space receives an available target-subnet IP address. You need to migrate the database to Azure. The solution must meet these requirements:

FCI1 hosts the database tier for an SAP NetWeaver system. The application tier connects to FCI1 by using the virtual network name (VNN) `fci1.contoso.com`. An Azure Private DNS zone provides name resolution.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a production SAP on Azure landscape hosted on Standard M-series virtual machines.  
  
You intend to increase the storage capacity of the virtual machines.  
  
Which disk type can be expanded without downtime?
questions.explanation:
Azure Premium SSD v2 managed disks do not use fixed tiers; their capacity, IOPS, and throughput can each be changed to any supported value on the fly, without detaching the disk from the virtual machine or causing any downtime. Premium SSD v1, Standard SSD, and Standard HDD disks, by contrast, require the disk to be unattached (typically by deallocating the VM) before the disk size can be expanded. This makes Premium SSD v2 the disk type on Standard M-series VMs whose capacity can be increased without interrupting the running SAP workload.

**Learn more:** [Scalability and performance targets for VM disks - Azure Virtual Machines | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/disks-scalability-targets)

You need to recommend an Azure support agreement for the deployment. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Receive support for moderate business-impact events within four hours.  
- Comply with the SAP support agreement.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
Which support level should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
The Standard Azure support plan is the lowest-cost plan designed for production workloads. It provides a four-hour response target for moderate business-impact (Severity B) incidents, while Professional Direct exceeds that response target at a higher cost. Basic and Developer do not provide the required production technical-support coverage.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Support Plans Comparison](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/support/plans/)

questions.domain: Maintain SAP workloads on Azure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an SAP production environment that uses SAP HANA databases on Azure.  
  
You need to deploy a disaster-recovery solution for the SAP HANA databases. The solution must satisfy the following requirements:  
  
- Support failover across Azure regions.  
- Minimize data loss if a failover occurs.  
  
What should you deploy?

options.text: HANA system replication that uses asynchronous replication
HANA system replication that uses synchronous replication

questions.explanation:
For SAP HANA databases on Azure VMs, native SAP HANA system replication is the appropriate replication technology. Across Azure regions, HANA system replication should use asynchronous replication because the latency and distance between regions make synchronous HANA replication unsuitable. This provides a secondary HANA system that can be taken over in the disaster-recovery region, with replication lag determining the potential data loss.

**Learn more:** [SAP HANA availability across Azure regions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/sap-hana-availability-across-regions) · [Disaster Recovery overview and infrastructure guidelines for SAP workload](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/disaster-recovery-overview-guide)

questions.domain: Design and implement an infrastructure to support SAP workloads on Azure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an SAP production landscape in Azure.  
  
You need to assess the performance of the virtual machines hosting the landscape and ensure that their configuration is suitable for the workload. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Center for SAP solutions provides a centralized management experience for SAP systems in Azure. Its Quality Insights capabilities provide VM-level performance metrics, including CPU, disk, network, and availability, and run configuration and quality checks against Azure and SAP best practices. This delivers SAP-specific assessment of VM performance and configuration with low administrative overhead.

**Learn more:** [Get quality checks and insights for a Virtual Instance for SAP solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/center-sap-solutions/get-quality-checks-insights) · [Azure Center for SAP solutions overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/center-sap-solutions/overview)

questions.question:
You have an on-premises SAP landscape and a hybrid Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You plan to enable Azure AD authentication for SAP NetWeaver.  
  
What should you configure in Azure AD first?
questions.explanation:
An SAP NetWeaver integration must first have an Azure AD enterprise application, represented by a service principal, so that SAML/OAuth authentication settings, user assignments, and claims can be configured. Microsoft’s SAP NetWeaver integration guidance begins by adding SAP NetWeaver from the gallery to the managed enterprise applications in the tenant.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure SAP NetWeaver for Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/saas-apps/sap-netweaver-tutorial)

questions.domain: Design and implement an infrastructure to support SAP workloads on Azure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises datacenter.  
  
You have an Azure subscription that contains a virtual network named VNet1.  
  
VNet1 uses forced tunneling to direct all outbound internet traffic through the datacenter.  
  
You deploy an SAP landscape to VNet1. The landscape uses virtual machines that run Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) and use pay-as-you-go rates.  
  
You discover that the virtual machines do not receive operating system updates.  
  
You need to ensure that the virtual machines receive operating system updates.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add user-defined routes (UDRs) to the route table.
Configure an Azure DNS Private Resolver.

questions.explanation:
RHEL pay-as-you-go virtual machines use Azure Red Hat Update Infrastructure (RHUI) for updates. With forced tunneling, RHUI traffic is sent through the on-premises network, which prevents the required Azure-originated connectivity to RHUI. User-defined routes for the RHUI IP addresses route that traffic appropriately so the VMs can receive updates.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot Red Hat RHUI connectivity issues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-machines/linux/linux-rhui-connectivity-issues) · [Red Hat Update Infrastructure for on-demand Red Hat Enterprise Linux VMs in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/workloads/redhat/redhat-rhui)

questions.domain: Migrate SAP workloads to Azure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to migrate a production SAP ERP Central Component (SAP ECC) system to Azure.  
  
You are reviewing the system's SAP EarlyWatch Alert report.  
  
You need to recommend Azure virtual machine sizes to host the system.  
  
Which two report sections should you review? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Patch Levels under SAP Software Configuration

questions.explanation:
Hardware Capacity provides the observed CPU and memory capacity/utilization needed to size compute, while Hardware Configuration under Landscape provides the current server hardware baseline. Azure SAP VM selection starts with CPU, memory, SAPS, and measured database I/O requirements, then maps them to VM family/SKU limits. SAP EarlyWatch Alert is designed to report hardware utilization and performance data.

**Learn more:** [Plan and implement an SAP deployment on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/planning-guide) · [SAP EarlyWatch Alert](https://support.sap.com/en/offerings-programs/support-services/earlywatch-alert.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an existing SAP landscape in Azure. All SAP virtual machines reside on the same virtual network. The SAP application servers, SAP management servers, and SAP database servers are each located on their own subnet.  
  
You need to ensure that only the application and management servers can access the subnet to which the database servers are connected.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Azure Application Gateway and firewall rules

questions.explanation:
Network security groups (NSGs) filter inbound and outbound traffic for resources in an Azure virtual network and can be associated with a subnet. An NSG applied to the database subnet can allow traffic from the application and management server subnets while denying traffic from other sources.

**Learn more:** [How Network Security Groups Filter Network Traffic in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-group-how-it-works)

questions.domain: Maintain SAP workloads on Azure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You require direct connectivity from an on-premises network to SAP HANA (Large Instances). The solution must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
- Provide the highest level of resiliency.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
ExpressRoute Global Reach links the customer ExpressRoute circuit with the SAP HANA Large Instances ExpressRoute circuit, enabling on-premises traffic to reach the HANA tenant directly without a separately administered proxy such as iptables. Microsoft recommends Global Reach for SAP HANA Large Instance deployments to provide direct on-premises access.

**Learn more:** [SAP workload networking and connectivity - Microsoft Azure Well-Architected Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/sap/design-areas/networking-and-connectivity) · [Connectivity setup from virtual machines to SAP HANA on Azure (Large Instances)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/large-instances/archived-hli-docs/hana-connect-azure-vm-large-instances)

questions.domain: Design and implement high availability and disaster recovery (HADR)
questions.question:
You have an Azure SAP HANA (Large Instances) instance named HLI1 with storage volume snapshots enabled.  
  
You need to monitor HLI1 storage usage. The solution must monitor:  
  
- The number of stored snapshots  
- The storage consumed by the snapshots  
  
Which Linux OS command should you use?
questions.explanation:
The `du` command reports disk usage for a directory tree, so it can measure the storage consumed by snapshot directories and provide per-directory results for the stored snapshots. `ls` only lists directory entries and does not calculate their disk consumption. Microsoft documents that Azure Large Instance snapshot details include individual snapshot sizes and the total size used by snapshots.\
\
**Learn more:** [Obtain details using Azure Application Consistent Snapshot tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-netapp-files/azacsnap-cmd-ref-details)

questions.question:
You intend to deploy an SAP landscape on Azure. The landscape will use SAP HANA databases running on Azure virtual machines. It will include four Azure virtual machines that will have the SAP Web Dispatcher role.  
  
You need to minimize network latency between the web dispatcher virtual machines and the HANA virtual machines.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Enable Accelerated Networking on the virtual machines.
Enable large send offload on the virtual machines.

questions.explanation:
Azure Accelerated Networking uses SR-IOV on supported virtual machine types to provide a high-performance network path that bypasses the host virtual switch, reducing latency and jitter between virtual machines.\

options.text: SAP HANA hardware and cloud measurement tools

You need to estimate the number of SAP operations the landscape will process each hour. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Backup supports scheduled backup for SAP HANA databases running on Azure virtual machines and supports backup of Azure VMs. It does not support Azure NetApp Files volumes or NFS Azure file shares as Azure Backup sources, and Application Gateway configuration is not a supported Azure Backup workload.

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing two virtual machines configured as a Pacemaker cluster. The cluster hosts a highly available SAP HANA deployment.  
  
Which command should you use to configure the Pacemaker cluster's failover behavior?
questions.explanation:
The `crm` command is Pacemaker’s cluster-management interface and is used to configure cluster resources, constraints, properties, fencing, and related failover behavior. Microsoft’s SAP HANA high-availability guidance uses `crm configure` commands to define these Pacemaker settings.\

You have an Azure subscription containing two virtual machines configured as a Pacemaker cluster. The cluster hosts a highly available SAP HANA deployment.  
  
Which command should you use to configure the Pacemaker cluster's failover behavior?

options.text: a Hybrid Runbook Worker in Azure Automation
auto registration for the private DNS zone

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are assessing which migration approach Litware can implement, based on the current environment and business objectives.  
  
Which migration method causes the least downtime?

options.text: Migrate SAP ECC to SAP Business Suite in HANA, and then migrate SAP to Azure.
Use Near-Zero Downtime (NZDT) to migrate to SAP HANA and Azure during the same maintenance window.
Use the Database Migration Option (DMO) to migrate to SAP HANA and Azure during the same maintenance window.
Migrate SAP to Azure, and then migrate SAP ECC to SAP Business Suite on HANA.

questions.explanation:
SAP Near-Zero Downtime Technology (NZDT) is specifically intended to optimize migration downtime. Combining the migration to SAP HANA and Azure within the same maintenance window avoids the additional outage associated with separate, sequential migrations.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning a small-scale deployment of an SAP HANA on Azure (Large Instances) landscape.  
  
You determine the costs of the virtual machine SKU needed to host the HANA Large Instances landscape.  
  
Which additional costs will you incur?

options.text: an ExpressRoute circuit between the HANA Large Instances stamp and Azure
a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the HANA Large Instances stamp and Azure
an Azure Rapid Response support contract

questions.explanation:
SAP HANA on Azure (Large Instances) uses an ExpressRoute circuit between the Azure subscription and the HANA Large Instance stamp. ExpressRoute has its own circuit and, where applicable, gateway and data-transfer charges, separate from the HANA Large Instance SKU.

**Learn more:** [Connectivity setup from virtual machines to SAP HANA on Azure (Large Instances)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/large-instances/archived-hli-docs/hana-connect-azure-vm-large-instances) · [Plan to manage costs for Azure ExpressRoute](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/plan-manage-cost)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing multiple virtual machines. The virtual machines host an SAP non-production landscape in Azure.  
  
You need to configure the virtual machines to stop and start at specified times. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Automation account can run scheduled runbooks that start and stop targeted virtual machines. Azure Automation schedules support recurring execution, allowing centralized, low-administration management of the non-production landscape.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You migrate an on-premises SAP HANA instance that runs SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES) to an Azure virtual machine.  
  
You expect that, in two years, you will replace the virtual machine with a larger virtual machine in the same flexibility group.  
  
You need to recommend solutions that minimize HANA deployment costs over the next three years. The solutions must not affect the availability SLAs.  
  
Which two solutions should you recommend? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a three-year reservation that has instance size flexibility
a one-year reservation that has capacity priority
a one-year reservation that has instance size flexibility

questions.explanation:
A three-year Azure VM reservation provides discounted pricing for the complete three-year period, and instance size flexibility allows its benefit to apply across eligible VM sizes in the same flexibility group. Azure Hybrid Benefit for Linux supports bringing an existing SLES subscription to Azure, so the SLES software fee is covered by that subscription while Azure infrastructure charges remain. Both approaches reduce cost without changing the running VM’s availability SLA.

**Learn more:** [Instance size flexibility for Azure Reservations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/reservations/instance-size-flexibility) · [Azure Hybrid Benefit for Linux virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/azure-hybrid-benefit-linux)

You plan to migrate this environment to Azure by using Azure Site Recovery.

What should you deploy first?

Microsoft System Center Virtual Machine Manager (VMM)

Your on-premises network connects to an SAP HANA deployment in the East US Azure region. The deployment uses the Standard SKU of an ExpressRoute gateway.

You plan to migrate the ERP system to SAP Business Suite on SAP HANA running on Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to determine the appropriate sizing for Business Suite on HANA.

options.text: SAP Quick Sizer for HANA Cloud

questions.explanation:
SAP HANA Quick Sizer is the SAP sizing tool for workloads that use SAP HANA as their database, including Business Suite on HANA. The HANA Cloud variant is intended for products that run as SAP cloud offerings, whereas this deployment runs on Azure virtual machines.\

**Learn more:** [SAP Sizing](https://www.sap.com/about/benchmark/sizing.html) · [Sizing SAP HANA](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_HANA_PLATFORM/eb3777d5495d46c5b2fa773206bbfb46/d4a122a7bb57101493e3f5ca08e6b039.html)

You plan to migrate the ERP system to SAP Business Suite on SAP HANA running on Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to determine the appropriate sizing for Business Suite on HANA.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Configure scaling of Azure App Service
Migrate the SQL Server databases to Azure SQL Data Warehouse
Deallocate virtual machines when not in use
Deploy non-production landscapes to Azure DevTest Labs

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to deploy an SAP environment in Azure.  
  
You plan to securely store all SAP connection strings in Azure Key Vault, without keeping credentials on the Azure virtual machines that host SAP.  
  
What should you configure to enable the virtual machines to access the key vault?

options.text: Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privilege Identity Manager (PIM)

questions.explanation:
A Managed Service Identity (MSI), now termed a managed identity, gives an Azure virtual machine an automatically managed Microsoft Entra identity. The VM can use that identity to obtain a token for Azure Key Vault without storing credentials locally; the identity must also receive the necessary Key Vault secret permissions.

**Learn more:** [Use a Linux VM system-assigned managed identity to access Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/tutorial-linux-managed-identities-vm-access) · [Tutorial: Use Azure Key Vault with a virtual machine in Python](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/tutorial-python-virtual-machine)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning an SAP on Azure deployment that will use SAP HANA.  
  
You need to ensure that the SAP application servers are located in the same datacenter as the HANA nodes.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
An Azure proximity placement group applies a colocation constraint to compute resources, placing them in the same datacenter or network spine to minimize physical distance and network latency. Microsoft’s SAP guidance specifically identifies proximity placement groups for keeping SAP application servers and database resources close together.

**Learn more:** [Configuration options to minimize network latency with SAP applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/proximity-placement-scenarios) · [Proximity placement groups - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/co-location)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an SAP production landscape in Azure.  
  
Users access the landscape from the internet through Azure Application Gateway.  
  
You need to analyze the landscape’s network traffic by using Azure Network Watcher Traffic Analytics.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Azure Network Watcher Traffic Analytics analyzes flow-log data to provide insights into cloud network traffic. NSG flow logs record IP traffic processed by a network security group and can be enabled for Traffic Analytics, making them the required configuration among the available choices. Current Azure guidance recommends virtual network flow logs for new deployments, but that option is not available here.

**Learn more:** [Traffic Analytics Overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/traffic-analytics) · [Create, change, enable, disable, or delete NSG flow logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/nsg-flow-logs-manage)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Monitor for SAP solutions resource and a virtual machine named VM1. VM1 runs SUSE Enterprise Linux (SLES) and hosts an SAP NetWeaver application server.  
  
You need to use the Azure Monitor for SAP solutions resource to monitor VM1's CPU, memory, and network usage.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: On VM1, install the Prometheus node exporter.
From the Azure portal, add the Azure Monitor for SAP solutions NetWeaver provider.

questions.explanation:

An Azure proximity placement group places the VM resources physically close together under the same network spine, minimizing this latency and thereby reducing accumulated database-access time.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to deploy an SAP landscape on Azure that uses SAP HANA on Azure (Large Instances).  
  
You must ensure that outbound traffic from the application tier can flow only to the database tier.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Network security groups (NSGs) enforce inbound and outbound network filtering rules on Azure subnets or network interfaces, enabling the application tier to be restricted to database-tier destinations. Microsoft guidance for SAP workloads specifies that traffic-routing restrictions to and from DBMS virtual machines are defined by NSGs and recommends NSGs with application security groups for granular tier-based rules.

Solution: Configure a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN connection between the datacenter and VNet1, and another S2S VPN connection between VNet1 and the managed workload.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Site-to-Site VPN tunnels alone do not guarantee transitive connectivity between the datacenter, VNet1, and the SAP RISE managed workload. Azure VPN Gateway uses BGP route propagation to provide transit routing across multiple connected networks; without that routing configuration, the required end-to-end connectivity is not ensured.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure BGP for Azure VPN Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/bgp-howto) · [Network connectivity options in Azure with SAP RISE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/rise-integration-network)

Solution: Configure a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN connection between the datacenter and the managed workload, and configure virtual network peering between VNet1 and the managed workload.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Virtual network peering is not transitive. To allow VNet1 to reach an on-premises datacenter through an S2S VPN gateway in a peered network, the peering must be configured for gateway transit, including allowing gateway transit on the gateway network and using remote gateways on VNet1. A standard S2S VPN connection plus peering does not provide that connectivity by itself.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Network peering overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-peering-overview) · [Configure VPN gateway transit for virtual network peering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-peering-gateway-transit)

Does this meet the goal?

Virtual network peering is not transitive. A peered network can use an ExpressRoute gateway in the peer only when gateway transit is explicitly configured: the gateway VNet must allow gateway transit and the peered VNet must use remote gateways. A basic ExpressRoute connection to VNet1 plus virtual network peering does not provide the required end-to-end connectivity.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An on-premises SAP NetWeaver deployment uses Windows Server 2016 and Microsoft SQL Server 2016.  
  
You need to migrate the deployment to an Azure virtual machine running Windows Server 2016 with Microsoft SQL Server 2019 installed.  
  
Which migration method should be used?
questions.explanation:
SAP Database Migration Option (DMO), provided by Software Update Manager, combines an SAP system update with database migration in a single procedure and supports Microsoft SQL Server as the target database. It is appropriate when moving the SAP system while upgrading the SQL Server database from 2016 to 2019. A heterogeneous classical migration is intended for a change of operating system or database platform, neither of which occurs here.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a two-node SAP HANA cluster hosted on Azure virtual machines. Each cluster node uses Azure NetApp Files for database-file storage. The nodes replicate synchronously by using HANA system replication.  
  
You need to implement a backup solution for the HANA databases. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Be cluster-aware.  
- Support snapshots.  
- Ensure application-consistent backups.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
AzAcSnap orchestrates application-consistent Azure NetApp Files storage snapshots for SAP HANA. It prepares SAP HANA for the snapshot, creates snapshots for the configured data volumes, releases the database after completion, and manages SAP HANA backup-catalog activity. Its configuration supports SAP HANA instances across nodes, making it suitable for this clustered HANA deployment.

questions.explanation:
Azure Site Recovery can replicate SAP workloads to Azure, but it does not perform a database-platform conversion from Microsoft SQL Server to SAP HANA. Migrating an SAP system to SAP HANA requires a heterogeneous system copy or SAP Database Migration Option (DMO), which combines an SAP upgrade with migration to the SAP HANA database.\
\
**Learn more:** [Migrate an SAP platform to Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/scenarios/sap/migrate) · [General Information About the Migration to SAP HANA](https://help.sap.com/docs/r/673893cabe6f4359a76f0d41a301b4d5/CURRENT_VERSION/en-US/9e183a5312516757e10000000a44538d.html)

Solution: Deploy a new environment in Azure that uses SAP NetWeaver 7.4. Export the databases from the on-premises environment, then import the databases into the Azure environment.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A heterogeneous SAP system copy may change the operating system and database platform, but the source and target SAP system releases must be identical. A database export from SAP NetWeaver 7.0 cannot be directly imported as a system copy into a SAP NetWeaver 7.4 target; a supported release-upgrade process is also required.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Cases for System Copy](https://help.sap.com/docs/SLTOOLSET/6ffd9a3438944dc39dfe288d758a2ed5/f4a439531b87e547e10000000a441470.html)

Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Migrating an SAP system from Microsoft SQL Server to SAP HANA requires a database migration, typically a heterogeneous system copy using SAP migration tools. Azure Site Recovery moves the existing system but does not convert its SQL Server database to SAP HANA; a later SAP NetWeaver 7.4 upgrade alone also does not perform that database migration.\
\
**Learn more:** [General Information About the Migration to SAP HANA](https://help.sap.com/docs/r/673893cabe6f4359a76f0d41a301b4d5/CURRENT_VERSION/en-US/9e183a5312516757e10000000a44538d.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises server named Server1 that runs Windows Server and has the DNS Server role installed. Server1 hosts a DNS domain named contoso.com.  
  
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You have an SAP RISE managed workload that includes a DNS server named Server2.  
  
You need to ensure DNS name resolution functions across the on-premises, Azure, and SAP environments.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Delegate a domain named ecs.contoso.com to Server1.
Implement zone transfers between Server1 and Server2.
Configure a conditional forwarder on Server1.
Delegate a domain named ecs.contoso.com to Server2.

questions.explanation:
A child DNS namespace is made resolvable by creating a delegation in its parent zone. Because Server1 hosts the parent zone `contoso.com`, it must delegate `ecs.contoso.com` to Server2, the authoritative DNS server for that child namespace. DNS delegation records direct queries for the child zone to its designated name server.

**Learn more:** [Manage DNS zones using DNS server in Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/dns/manage-dns-zones)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises SAP NetWeaver deployment. It has a DB2 data store containing a 5-TB SAP database.  
  
You plan to migrate the deployment to SQL Server on an Azure virtual machine.  
  
You need to optimize transaction-log write performance during the migration. The solution must **not** affect the virtual machine's I/O quota.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Place the transaction logs on the temporary disk.
Place the transaction logs on a striped volume of Premium SSD disks.
Place the transaction logs on an Ultra disk.
Enable the write cache for the disk that hosts the transaction logs.

questions.explanation:
Ultra Disk is intended for I/O-intensive, latency-sensitive workloads such as transaction-heavy databases. An Ultra Disk-compatible VM allocates dedicated bandwidth between the compute instance and the block-storage scale unit, supporting high-performance transaction-log writes without relying on the VM’s regular disk I/O quota.

**Learn more:** [Select a disk type for Azure IaaS VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/disks-types) · [Storage performance best practices for SQL Server on Azure VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/performance-guidelines-best-practices-storage?view=azuresql)

You intend to deploy an SAP environment on Azure that will use Azure Availability Zones.  
  
Which load-balancing solution supports the deployment?
questions.explanation:

You intend to deploy an SAP production landscape that uses SAP HANA databases on Azure.  
  
You need to configure the storage infrastructure to support the SAP HANA deployment. The solution must meet SAP-issued data-throughput and I/O requirements.  
  
How should you configure the storage?
questions.explanation:
RAID 0 stripes I/O across multiple disks, increasing aggregate throughput and IOPS to satisfy SAP HANA storage performance requirements. Microsoft’s Azure guidance identifies striped disk volumes as a way to improve I/O performance for SAP HANA workloads.\

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy a production SAP landscape in Azure.  
  
You need to choose a support plan. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Respond to critical-impact incidents within one hour.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should you select?
questions.explanation:
Azure Standard support provides a one-hour response time for critical business-impact (Sev A) incidents. It is the lowest-cost paid Azure support plan that meets this requirement; Professional Direct provides the same critical-incident response time at a higher price, while Basic does not include technical support.\
\

You need to encrypt VM1. The solution must satisfy the following requirements:  
  
- All disks must be encrypted.  
- The effect on VM1 CPU must be minimized.  
- Manual rotation of encryption keys must be supported.  
  
Which encryption type should you use?

options.text: Encryption at rest with platform-managed keys
Encryption at rest with customer-managed keys

questions.explanation:
Encryption at host encrypts data at the VM host, including temporary disks and OS/data disk caches, and encrypts the data as it flows to Azure Storage. It does not use the VM’s CPU or affect VM performance. When combined with customer-managed keys through a disk encryption set, it supports encryption-key rotation. Azure Disk Encryption performs guest-level encryption and consumes guest VM resources.

**Learn more:** [Server-side encryption of Azure managed disks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/disk-encryption) · [Enable end-to-end encryption using encryption at host](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/disks-enable-host-based-encryption-cli)

questions.question:
You plan to deploy an SAP landscape that will include virtual machines deployed across multiple Azure regions.  
  
You need to ensure that the virtual machines can communicate between the regions.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Azure virtual network peering—specifically global VNet peering for different regions—connects virtual networks across Azure regions and permits resources, including virtual machines, to communicate privately over the Microsoft backbone network.\
\

questions.question:
You are designing a production SAP on Azure landscape.  
  
The landscape must maintain service availability if an Azure datacenter fails.  
  
What should be included in the design?
questions.explanation:
Availability zones use physically separate datacenters with independent power, cooling, and networking. Deploying workload components across zones provides resilience to a datacenter failure; availability sets address more localized hardware and maintenance failures within a datacenter.\
\
**Learn more:** [What are Azure availability zones?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/availability-zones-overview) · [Regions and zones on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/aws-professional/regions-zones)

The landscape must maintain service availability if an Azure datacenter fails.  
  
What should be included in the design?

options.text: Azure Migrate and SAP EarlyWatch Alert reports
Azure Site Recovery and SAP Quick Sizer
SAP Quick Sizer and SAP HANA system replication
Azure Site Recovery Deployment Planner and SAP HANA Cockpit

questions.explanation:
Azure Migrate discovers VMware-managed servers through vCenter and collects configuration and performance metadata used to assess and size Azure resources. SAP EarlyWatch Alert reports supply SAP-specific workload and utilization data, enabling the Azure compute requirements for the SAP landscape to be identified.

questions.question:
An SAP HANA virtual machine performs daily backups to a container in an Azure Storage account.  
  
You need the backups older than 30 days to be deleted automatically.  
  
What type of policy should you create?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage lifecycle management policies can automatically delete blobs when they reach a specified age, so a rule can remove backup files after 30 days.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-overview) · [Lifecycle management policies that delete blobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-policy-delete)

questions.question:
You have an SAP NetWeaver deployment hosted on Azure virtual machines running SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES), configured as a Pacemaker cluster.  
  
You need to monitor the deployment by using Azure Monitor for SAP Solutions.  
  
What should you install first on the cluster nodes?
questions.explanation:
For a SUSE-based Pacemaker cluster, Azure Monitor for SAP Solutions requires the `ha_cluster_provider` HA agent to be installed on every cluster node. Performance Co-Pilot, `pcp-pmda-hacluster`, and `pmproxy` apply to RHEL-based clusters.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create a high-availability Pacemaker cluster provider for Azure Monitor for SAP solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/monitor/provider-ha-pacemaker-cluster)

questions.question:
You have an on-premises SAP NetWeaver landscape that includes an IBM DB2 database.  
  
You need to migrate the database to a Microsoft SQL Server instance running on an Azure virtual machine.  
  
Which tool should you use?
questions.explanation:
SQL Server Migration Assistant (SSMA) for Db2 is designed to migrate IBM Db2 databases to SQL Server. It converts Db2 database objects for the SQL Server target and supports migrating the data; SQL Server running on an Azure virtual machine remains a SQL Server target.\
\
**Learn more:** [SQL Server Migration Assistant](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/ssma/sql-server-migration-assistant?view=sql-server-ver17)

You need to migrate the database to a Microsoft SQL Server instance running on an Azure virtual machine.  
  
Which tool should you use?

options.text: Microsoft System Center 2019 - Data Protection Manager (DPM 2019)

questions.explanation:
Azure Data Box supports secure offline transfer of large on-premises datasets into Azure. It is appropriate for seeding the 30-TB SQL Server database without relying on the 500-Mbps ExpressRoute circuit for the full initial data transfer.

questions.question:
You have a managed SAP RISE workload.  
  
You plan to implement Microsoft Security Copilot for RISE.  
  
Which Security Copilot plug-in should you configure to support this implementation?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Security Copilot can use SAP RISE/ECS data through Microsoft Sentinel. The Microsoft Sentinel solution for SAP applications is deployed in the customer’s Azure subscription to ingest and analyze SAP security signals, while Azure Monitor for SAP solutions and Azure Center for SAP solutions are not supported for SAP RISE/ECS.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure identity and security services with SAP RISE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/rise-integration-security)

You have an on-premises SAP landscape hosted on VMware vSphere that contains 50 virtual machines.  
  
You need to perform a lift-and-shift migration to Azure by using Azure Migrate. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you deploy first?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Migrate configuration server is the initial on-premises component for the VMware agent-based migration architecture. It coordinates communication and replication between VMware and Azure, and an integrated process server can handle the workload, avoiding deployment of a separate process server for this environment.\

Each landscape includes virtual machines that run the following:  
  
- SAP HANA  
- SAP NetWeaver  
- Microsoft SQL Server  
  
You need to monitor the landscapes while minimizing costs.  
  
What is the minimum number of required Azure Monitor for SAP Solutions instances?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Monitor for SAP solutions resource supports multiple provider types and multiple providers of the same type. A single instance deployed in VNET1 can therefore use providers to collect data from the SAP HANA, SAP NetWeaver, and SQL Server components in both connected landscapes. The minimum required number of instances is one.

options.text: a zone-redundant public IP address for the internal load balancer
a zone-redundant frontend IP address for the internal Azure Basic Load Balancer
a zone-redundant frontend IP address for the internal Azure Standard Load Balancer

questions.explanation:
A Standard internal Azure Load Balancer frontend is created because the configuration uses the Standard SKU and assigns a private IP address in a subnet. What should you use to export data from DB2 and import it into SQL Server?

You have an Azure subscription and an Enterprise Agreement (EA).  
  
You plan to deploy an SAP on Azure production landscape containing these virtual machines:  
  
- One M-series virtual machine with 128 cores  
- 15 E-series virtual machines with a combined total of 300 cores  
- 10 D-series virtual machines with a combined total of 160 cores  
  
While deploying the E-series virtual machines, you receive this error message:  
  
`Operation results in exceeding quota limits of Core.`  
  
You need to ensure that you can complete the E-series virtual machine deployment. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Maintain the SAP landscape performance.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a second subscription and split the virtual machines evenly between both subscriptions.
Resize the D-series and E-series virtual machines.
Request a quota increase for the Azure region.

questions.explanation:
Azure enforces total regional vCPU quotas per subscription and region, as well as VM-family vCPU quotas. Requesting a regional quota increase allows the planned E-series deployment to proceed without changing the SAP VM sizing or splitting the environment across subscriptions, thereby preserving performance while minimizing administration and cost.

**Learn more:** [Increase regional vCPU quotas - Azure Quotas](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/quotas/regional-quota-requests) · [Check vCPU quotas - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/quotas)

You intend to deploy a highly available SAP HANA system in a scale-out configuration with standby on Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to implement shared storage volumes using Azure NetApp Files.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Azure NetApp Files volumes must be deployed into a subnet delegated to Azure NetApp Files. The delegated subnet grants the service permission to create the service-specific networking resources required for the volumes; Private Link, private endpoints, and service endpoints are not the required initial resource.\
\

questions.question: What should you use to carry out load testing as part of the migration plan?
questions.explanation:
Apache JMeter is used to create and execute load tests that simulate application traffic. Azure Load Testing supports uploading and running Apache JMeter scripts at scale, whereas Azure Application Insights and Azure Monitor collect telemetry and monitor resources rather than perform load generation.\
\
**Learn more:** [Load test a website by using a JMeter script in Azure Load Testing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-testing/load-testing/how-to-create-and-run-load-test-with-jmeter-script) · [Build a migration plan with Azure Migrate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/concepts-migration-planning?view=migrate-classic)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to migrate an SAP environment to Azure.  
  
You need to design a solution that enables end-user access to SAP applications through the Internet while limiting user access to the virtual machines hosting the SAP application servers.  
  
What should the design include?

options.text: Configure a public IP address for each SAP application server
Deploy an internal Azure Standard Load Balancer for incoming connections
Use an SAP Web Dispatcher to route all incoming HTTP connections
Configure point-to-site VPN connections for each user

questions.explanation:
SAP Web Dispatcher provides an SAP-aware HTTP(S) entry point that routes and load-balances incoming web traffic to SAP application servers. This keeps the application-server virtual machines behind the dispatcher instead of exposing them directly to Internet users. Microsoft’s SAP-on-Azure guidance describes SAP Web Dispatcher as the component that provides application integration and routes web sessions to SAP systems.

**Learn more:** [Inbound and outbound internet connections for SAP on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/guide/sap/sap-internet-inbound-outbound) · [Run SAP BW/4HANA with Linux VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/reference-architectures/sap/run-sap-bw4hana-with-linux-virtual-machines)

You plan to migrate the environment to Azure, while keeping the same database platform.

The SAP EarlyWatch Alert report provides performance, workload, and capacity information for an existing SAP system. You have an SAP RISE managed workload.  
  
You need to configure connectivity from VNet1 to SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP).  
  
What should the solution include?

options.text: SAP Private Link service for Azure

questions.explanation:
SAP Private Link service for Azure provides private connectivity between SAP BTP services and resources in an Azure subscription, using Azure Private Link rather than public internet routing. It is the suitable connectivity mechanism for an Azure virtual network and an SAP RISE managed workload communicating with SAP BTP.\
\

questions.explanation:
Azure Load Balancer Standard supports availability-zone and zone-redundant frontend configurations and can route traffic to healthy backend application servers across zones. With the two application servers in different zones, it preserves application-server access if one datacenter/availability zone fails. Azure Basic Load Balancer does not support availability zones.

You have an SAP RISE managed workload integrated with Sub1.

You need to mark particular users in the managed workload as sensitive while minimizing administrative effort.

You have an SAP landscape in Azure that uses SAP HANA.  
  
You back up HANA daily to Azure Blob Storage and retain a copy of every backup for one year.  
  
You need to lower backup-storage costs.  
  
What should you implement?

options.text: a Recovery Services Vault backup policy

questions.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage access tiers let infrequently accessed backup data be stored at a lower capacity cost. The archive tier is intended for long-term backups and archival datasets, making storage access tiering the applicable cost-reduction mechanism for one-year retained SAP HANA backups.\
\
**Learn more:** [Access tiers for blob data - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/access-tiers-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two Azure virtual machines named VM1 and VM2. VM1 hosts a single container database (SDC) for the SAP HANA instance named sd1. VM2 hosts an SDC HANA instance named sd2. Azure Backup is enabled for the HANA databases on VM1 and VM2.  
  
You need to restore sd1 to sd2 and overwrite the database instance on VM2.  
  
What should you do first in the Azure portal?

options.text: From Restore Configuration, set Restored DB Name to sd1(sdc).
Upgrade sd2 to Multiple Container Database (MDC).
From Restore Configuration, set Restored DB Name to sd2(sdc).
Rename the SystemDB database of sd2.

questions.explanation:
For an SAP HANA single database container restore to another SDC instance, the restored database name must be the target instance ID in lowercase followed by `(sdc)`. Therefore, the target name must be `sd2(sdc)`; the existing target database can then be overwritten. Microsoft documents this SDC-specific naming requirement in its SAP HANA restore troubleshooting guidance.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot SAP HANA databases backup errors - Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-sap-hana-database-troubleshoot)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to deploy an SAP environment on Azure. The SAP environment will include production, development, and quality-assurance landscapes.  
  
You need to minimize the costs of operating the development and quality-assurance landscapes on Azure.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure scaling for Azure App Service
Create a scheduled task that runs the stopsap command
Configure Azure virtual machine scale sets
Create Azure Automation runbooks to stop, deallocate, and start Azure virtual machines

questions.explanation:
For development and test environments, Azure recommends using Azure Automation or Logic Apps to implement an automatic VM start-and-stop schedule. A runbook can stop and deallocate the SAP virtual machines when they are not needed, then start them on schedule; deallocation removes VM compute charges while the nonproduction systems are idle.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for virtual machine cost optimization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/cost-optimization-best-practices)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to migrate an SAP environment to Azure.  
  
You need to design an Azure network infrastructure that meets these requirements:  
  
- Prevent end users from accessing the database servers.  
- Isolate the application servers from the database servers.  
- Ensure end users can access the SAP systems over the Internet.  
- Minimize communication costs between the application servers and database servers.  
  
Which two actions should you include in the solution? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: In the same Azure virtual network, segregate the SAP application servers and database servers by using different subnets and network security groups.
Segregate the SAP application servers and database servers by using different Azure virtual networks.
Create a site-to-site VPN between the on-premises network and Azure.
Configure an internal Azure Standard Load Balancer for incoming connections.
Configure Azure Traffic Manager to route incoming connections.

questions.explanation:
Separate application and database subnets within the same virtual network can have network security groups that allow only the required application-to-database traffic, preventing direct end-user access to the database tier. This layout keeps the tiers in the same virtual network; Microsoft’s SAP guidance notes that database and application VMs can be separated by subnet in the same virtual network and that traffic between peered virtual networks is subject to transfer costs. Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS-based load balancer that directs Internet client requests to public-facing application endpoints. An internal Load Balancer does not provide Internet ingress.

**Learn more:** [Considerations for Azure VMs DBMS deployment for SAP workload](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/dbms-guide-general) · [Azure Traffic Manager overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/traffic-manager/traffic-manager-overview)

options.text: On VM1, stop the HANA instance.
From RSV1, select the items to back up.
On VM1, run the preregistration script.
On VM1, install the Azure Backup Plugin for HANA.

questions.explanation:
The SAP HANA preregistration script must be run on the HANA server, as root, to create or configure the backup user and enable Azure Backup to discover the HANA databases. The Azure Backup Plugin for HANA is installed by the Azure Backup service after this prerequisite; backup items can then be selected and protected. The HANA instance must be running for database discovery.

**Learn more:** [About SAP HANA database backup on Azure VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/sap-hana-database-about) · [Azure Backup architecture for SAP HANA Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/azure-backup-architecture-for-sap-hana-backup)

You have an SAP production landscape in Azure that uses a two-node Pacemaker cluster.  
  
You need to ensure the cluster automatically fails over during Azure scheduled events.  
  
What should you configure on each node?

options.text: the Azure VM extension for SAP

questions.explanation:
The Azure fence agent provides Pacemaker STONITH fencing through Azure APIs, allowing the cluster to isolate or restart an affected node and safely move clustered resources to the other node. Azure scheduled-event integration marks an affected node unhealthy so Pacemaker migrates resources before the Azure maintenance action occurs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up Pacemaker on SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES) in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/high-availability-guide-suse-pacemaker)

a premium storage account file share
a standard storage account file share

questions.question:
You have an SAP HANA on Azure (Large Instances) deployment with two Type II SKU nodes. Each node is provisioned in a different Azure region.  
  
You need to monitor storage replication for this deployment.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: an Azure site-to-site VPN that is route-based
an Azure site-to-site VPN that is policy-based

questions.explanation:
Azure ExpressRoute provides private connectivity between an on-premises datacenter and Azure, with supported circuit bandwidth options that include 5 Gbps. Global VNet peering connects virtual networks rather than an on-premises datacenter, and the listed site-to-site VPN alternatives do not provide the required conventional 5-Gbps capacity. A 5-Gbps ExpressRoute circuit therefore meets the requirement without selecting a higher-bandwidth circuit.

**Learn more:** [Azure ExpressRoute overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/expressroute-introduction)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy an SAP production landscape in Azure.  
  
You need Azure NetApp Files to serve as the storage solution for SAP HANA databases.  
  
How should you configure an application volume group to minimize latency?
questions.explanation:
A proximity placement group associates the SAP HANA compute placement with nearby Azure NetApp Files resources. The application volume group uses that association to find storage hardware close to the database servers, minimizing network latency.\
\
**Learn more:** [Requirements and considerations for Azure NetApp Files application volume group for SAP HANA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-netapp-files/application-volume-group-considerations)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1. Sub1 contains an SAP landscape monitored by using Azure Monitor and Azure Center for SAP solutions.  
  
You plan to migrate this landscape to an SAP RISE managed workload.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for collecting monitoring data after the migration. The solution must minimize the time required to obtain the latest data.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: Request outbound internet connectivity from the managed workload.
Register a virtual instance with Azure Center for SAP solutions.
Request the monitoring data from SAP.
Configure user-defined routes (UDRs) for Azure Monitor for SAP solutions.

questions.explanation:
SAP RISE/ECS does not support integration with Azure Monitor for SAP solutions or Azure Center for SAP solutions. SAP provides its own monitoring and reporting for the fully managed environment, so obtaining the monitoring data from SAP is the supported approach with the most direct access to current data.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy SAP on Azure.  
  
You need to recommend a disk-encryption solution for virtual machines. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Support encryption of operating system, data, and temporary disks.  
- Support encryption of data at rest and in transit.  
- Minimize CPU overhead on the virtual machines.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Encryption at host encrypts temporary disks as well as OS and data disk caches at rest, and the encrypted data flows to Azure Storage. The encryption is performed on the VM host rather than inside the guest VM, so it does not use VM CPU or affect VM performance.

**Learn more:** [Server-side encryption of Azure managed disks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/disk-encryption) · [Overview of managed disk encryption options](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/disk-encryption-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy an SAP landscape that will store `/sapmnt` on an NFS Azure file share.  
  
You need to recommend a backup solution for `/sapmnt`. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Provide recoverability if the file share is deleted.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Backup currently does not support Azure file shares that use the NFS protocol. Azure Files share snapshots provide point-in-time recovery with minimal operational overhead. When file-share soft delete is enabled, a deleted share—including its contents and snapshots—can be restored during the retention period.

**Learn more:** [Support matrix for Azure Files backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/azure-file-share-support-matrix) · [Azure file share soft delete](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/storage-files-prevent-file-share-deletion)

Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The `M_LOAD_HISTORY_HOST` system view contains host load-history KPIs, including CPU utilization and timestamps. Querying it from SAP HANA Studio with a time filter for the prior 24 hours retrieves the required CPU metrics.\

**Learn more:** [M_LOAD_HISTORY_HOST System View](https://help.sap.com/docs/hana-cloud-database/sap-hana-cloud-sap-hana-database-sql-reference-guide/m-load-history-host-system-view)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure DB13 to back up directly to a local disk.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A backup written directly to a local disk remains on the SAP HANA host and is not an Azure backup. Backing up SAP HANA to Azure requires an Azure-integrated backup target, such as a Backint-based Azure Backup configuration or storage in Azure.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage backed up SAP HANA databases using Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/sap-hana-database-manage)

questions.question:
Solution: You use DBA Cockpit through SAP GUI.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
SAP HANA DBA Cockpit Load History provides historical performance KPIs for SAP HANA hosts and services and lets an administrator select the displayed time period. CPU utilization metrics for the preceding 24 hours can therefore be gathered through DBA Cockpit.\
\
**Learn more:** [SAP Help Portal — Load History (DBA Cockpit for SAP HANA)](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_NETWEAVER_DBOS/6b8fe8492ce14d24af5855c3d10701e3/6150e80fe56642d59c1544cb4cf0df69.html)

questions.question:
Solution: Use a third-party tool that uses backint to back up the SAP HANA database to Azure Storage.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
SAP HANA on Azure Large Instances supports customer-managed database backup strategies, including third-party backup solutions. Backint is SAP HANA’s native backup interface, and sending the resulting backups to Azure Storage satisfies the requirement to back up the database to Azure.\
\
**Learn more:** [SAP HANA on Azure Large Instance migration to Azure virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/large-instances/hana-large-instance-virtual-machine-migration) · [Operations model and responsibilities for SAP HANA on Azure Large Instances](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/large-instances/archived-hli-docs/hana-operations-model)

questions.question:

Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation: SAP HANA Quick Sizer estimates required system capacity; it does not collect historical CPU metrics from an SAP HANA instance. Gathering CPU utilization for the last 24 hours requires monitoring or performance-data collection from the running instance.

questions.domain: Maintain SAP workloads on Azure
questions.question:
Solution: You use **Monitoring** from the SAP HANA Cockpit.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?

SAP HANA Cockpit’s Performance Monitor displays historical CPU performance KPIs and supports selecting the monitored time frame, including the last 24 hours.\
\
**Learn more:** [The Performance Monitor | SAP Help Portal](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_HANA_COCKPIT/afa922439b204e9caf22c78b6b69e4f2/910353c47c7c4239857c94d14896ea43.html)

questions.question:
Solution: Back up directly to disk, copy the backups to an Azure virtual machine, and then copy the backups to an Azure Storage account.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
SAP HANA on Azure Large Instances is a dedicated bare-metal service, while Azure Backup’s SAP HANA workload protection is supported for SAP HANA running in Azure virtual machines. Manually copying disk backup files through a VM to a storage account does not provide the supported Azure Backup workflow for the HANA Large Instance database.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Backup support matrix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-support-matrix) · [SAP HANA on Azure Large Instance migration to Azure virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/large-instances/hana-large-instance-virtual-machine-migration)

\

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are migrating SAP to Azure. The ASCS application servers are located in one Azure zone, while the SAP database server is in a different Azure zone. ASCS/ERS is configured for high availability.  
  
During performance testing, you identify increased response times in Azure, although the Azure environment has better compute and memory configurations than the on-premises environment.  
  
During the initial analysis, you identify an increased Enqueue wait time.  
  
What are three possible causes of the increased wait time? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: disk I/O during Enqueue backup operations
misconfigured load balancer rules and health check probes for Enqueue and ASCS
network latency between the database server and the SAP application servers

questions.explanation:
Incorrect load-balancer rules or health probes can prevent reliable access to the ASCS/Enqueue virtual endpoint and lead to blocked or retried enqueue connections. Active enqueue replication can delay new enqueue requests when replication work backs up; SAP documents that the enqueue server throttles new requests when its replication queue becomes sufficiently full. Network round-trip latency between SAP application servers and a database placed in another availability zone increases transaction time and can prolong lock holding and enqueue waits.

**Learn more:** [Configuration options to minimize network latency with SAP applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/proximity-placement-scenarios) · [High Availability with the Standalone Enqueue Server](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_ON-PREMISE/78d0b136c1c8475f8dabbdd42debf47c/b583d98c22394d6e83a746a0d025529f.html?locale=en-US&state=PRODUCTION&version=2023.latest)

Before migrating, you must check source-system hardware utilization, including CPU, memory, network, and so on.

options.text: Redeploy the NetWeaver, application, and SQL Server virtual machines to the same proximity placement group.
Increase the tempdb size on the SQL Server virtual machines.
Configure the SQL Server database to use asynchronous replication.
Move the application virtual machines to the same subnet as the SQL Server virtual machines.

questions.explanation:
SAP NetWeaver is sensitive to network latency between the application and database tiers because application servers issue database queries at high frequency. An Azure proximity placement group places the related virtual machines close together under the same network spine, reducing network round-trip latency and therefore database-access time.

**Learn more:** [Configuration options to minimize network latency with SAP applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/proximity-placement-scenarios) · [Proximity placement groups - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/co-location)

questions.question:
You are assessing the migration plan.  
  
Licensing for which SAP product could be affected by resizing the virtual machines?
questions.explanation:
SAP ECC is the core application workload whose required capacity is sized in SAPS and CPU resources. Changing the virtual-machine size can change the available application capacity, which can affect the SAP ECC licensing position. Microsoft’s SAP-on-Azure planning guidance identifies SAP ECC as an SAP component and requires VM sizing to account for CPU and SAPS requirements.\

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning to deploy an SAP production landscape in Azure over the next three years. The deployment will use on-demand capacity reservations.  
  
You need to minimize the cost of the planned deployment.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Reserved VM Instances provide discounted pricing for a one-year or three-year commitment and can be applied to on-demand capacity reservations. On-demand capacity reservations otherwise incur pay-as-you-go charges for the underlying VM size, whether capacity is used or unused.

**Learn more:** [On-demand capacity reservation in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/capacity-reservation-overview) · [What are Azure Reservations?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/reservations/save-compute-costs-reservations)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Hyper-V generation 2 virtual-machine image that was prepared by running `sysprep.exe`.  
  
You plan to use the image as part of an SAP application-server deployment on Azure.  
  
You need to ensure that the image can be deployed as an Azure virtual machine.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Convert the virtual disk to a dynamically expanding disk.
Use Azure Storage Explorer to upload the VHDX file to a storage account.
Convert the VHDX disk image to a VHD disk image.
Run azcopy to upload the VHDX file to a managed disk.

questions.explanation:
Azure supports generation 2 virtual machines when their disks are fixed-size VHD files. A VHDX image must therefore be converted to VHD before it can be uploaded and used to deploy an Azure virtual machine. A dynamically expanding disk is not acceptable for this purpose.

**Learn more:** [Prepare a Windows VHD or VHDX to upload to Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/prepare-for-upload-vhd-image)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You migrate an SAP environment to Azure.  
  
You need to examine all outbound traffic from the SAP application servers to the Internet.  
  
Which two Azure resources should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a Web Application Firewall (WAF) for Azure Application Gateway

questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall centrally inspects and filters outbound network traffic. User-defined routes can send the default route (`0.0.0.0/0`) from the application-server subnets to the firewall, ensuring Internet-bound traffic traverses it for inspection.

**Learn more:** [Azure Firewall and traffic inspection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/azure-firewall) · [Deploy and configure Azure Firewall using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/tutorial-firewall-deploy-portal)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to deploy six Azure virtual machines that will host SAP application servers. The virtual machines will be distributed equally across three availability zones within a single Azure region.  
  
You must ensure that the two virtual machines in every zone are deployed on separate physical racks in a datacenter.  
  
Which two actions should you perform in each zone? Each correct answer provides part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Assign a different subnet to the network interface card of each virtual machine.
Configure each virtual machine to use a different storage account for the disks.
Place each pair of virtual machines in the same availability set.
Configure each virtual machine to use a different storage account for diagnostics.
Place each pair of virtual machines in the same proximity placement group.

questions.explanation:
Availability sets distribute their virtual machines across fault domains, which isolate underlying physical infrastructure such as power sources and network switches and provide the rack-level fault isolation required. A proximity placement group keeps the pair physically close; this is relevant because a single availability zone can span multiple physical datacenters. Microsoft’s SAP on Azure guidance describes combining availability sets and availability zones by using proximity placement groups.

**Learn more:** [Availability sets overview - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/availability-set-overview) · [Plan and implement an SAP deployment on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/planning-guide)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that includes a virtual network named VNet1.  
  
An SAP landscape in Azure is deployed in VNet1.  
  
You need to integrate the SAP landscape with SAP RISE. The solution must minimize costs.  
  
Which connection type should you use?
questions.explanation:
Virtual network peering is the preferred connectivity method between an existing customer Azure environment and SAP RISE/ECS. It provides direct private connectivity between the virtual networks and avoids the additional complexity and cost of a dedicated VPN or ExpressRoute path.\
\
**Learn more:** [Network connectivity options in Azure with SAP RISE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/rise-integration-network)

questions.question:
You have an SAP production environment in Azure, hosted on 50 virtual machines running SUSE Enterprise Linux (SLES). The virtual machines are billed at pay-as-you-go rates.  
  
You need to reduce the operating system costs of the virtual machines.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Hybrid Benefit for Linux can convert eligible SLES virtual machines from pay-as-you-go software billing to bring-your-own-subscription billing. The existing SLES subscription covers the software fee, so Azure charges only the VM infrastructure cost.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Hybrid Benefit for Linux virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/azure-hybrid-benefit-linux)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an SAP production landscape in Azure.  
  
You plan to migrate the landscape to a managed SAP RISE workload.  
  
Which task will become the exclusive responsibility of the SAP vendor after the migration?

options.text: configuring security monitoring in Microsoft Sentinel
sizing the Azure resources that host the landscape

questions.explanation:
SAP RISE runs the SAP landscape in an SAP-owned Azure subscription, where SAP manages the Azure resources and the technical architecture used for the managed workload. Security-monitoring integrations, single sign-on, and network peering are customer integration responsibilities. [Integrate Azure with SAP RISE managed workloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/rise-integration)
