lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an SAP deployment on Azure.  
  
You need to ensure that you can perform these tasks from the Azure portal:  
  
- View the status of SAP services.  
- Start and stop SAP services.  
  
The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Center for SAP solutions provides a unified Azure portal experience for registered SAP systems. It exposes SAP health and status information and supports starting and stopping the SAP application tier and individual SAP instances, satisfying both management requirements with minimal administration.

**Learn more:** [Register an existing SAP system](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/center-sap-solutions/register-existing-system) · [Start and stop SAP systems, instances, and HANA database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/center-sap-solutions/start-stop-sap-systems)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that includes an Azure logic app named App1.  
  
An SAP RISE managed workload is integrated with Sub1.  
  
You need to ensure that App1 can access data stored in SAP by using REST API calls.  
  
What should you deploy?
questions.explanation:
SAP RISE/ECS REST API access uses HTTPS and can be exposed through an application gateway. An integration runtime is intended for Azure Data Factory or Synapse data integration, while an on-premises data gateway supports SAP legacy RFC-based connectivity rather than REST API calls.\
\
**Learn more:** [Integrate Azure services with SAP RISE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/rise-integration-services)

questions.question:
You have an SAP landscape running on Azure.  
  
You deploy an SAP Web Dispatcher named web1.  
  
You need to verify that web1 can support 1,500 users.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Apache JMeter is a load-testing tool that can simulate virtual users and generate HTTP(S) workload against SAP Web Dispatcher to validate whether it handles the required 1,500-user load. Iometer and FIO assess storage I/O performance rather than web-user capacity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Stress test - SAP Analytics Cloud – BW Live Connection with jMeter](https://help.sap.com/docs/SUPPORT_CONTENT/boc/3354605732.html) · [Supported Apache JMeter features - Azure Load Testing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-testing/load-testing/resource-jmeter-support)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains two virtual machines hosting an SAP workload.  
  
You need to protect the workload by using Azure Site Recovery. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Support shared application-consistent recovery points.  
- Support shared crash-consistent recovery points.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Site Recovery replication group enables multi-VM consistency. Virtual machines in the group have shared crash-consistent and application-consistent recovery points at failover, providing coordinated recovery for the workload without requiring custom automation.

**Learn more:** [Common questions about Azure-to-Azure disaster recovery — Multi-VM consistency](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/site-recovery/azure-to-azure-common-questions#multi-vm-consistency)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an SAP landscape on Azure.

You need to collect those logs in Azure Monitor by using a Data Collection Rule (DCR). The solution must ensure that the logs are not sent over the internet.  
  
Which two resources should you configure? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor Private Link Scope (AMPLS) defines the private-link boundary for Azure Monitor resources. When the Azure Monitor Agent uses AMPLS, every associated Data Collection Rule must use a Data Collection Endpoint (DCE), and that DCE must be added to the AMPLS configuration. This routes DCR configuration and log-ingestion traffic through private connectivity rather than the public internet.

Your on-premises network has a 100-Mbps internet connection and includes an SAP production landscape with 14 TB of data files.  
  
You plan to migrate the on-premises SAP landscape to Azure.  
  
You need to transfer the data files to an Azure Files share. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Migrate the files within seven days.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
- Minimize service outages.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Data Box provides offline bulk transfer for data volumes that cannot reasonably traverse a 100-Mbps internet connection within seven days. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to automate deployment of SAP NetWeaver on Azure virtual machines by using Azure Resource Manager templates. The database tier will contain two Azure Marketplace Microsoft SQL Server 2017 virtual machine-image instances, each with 8 TB of RAM.  
  
Which task should be included in the templates that deploy the SQL Server virtual machines?

options.text: Enable read caching on the disks used to store the SQL Server database log files.
Run the SQL Server setup and specify the /ACTION=INSTALL and /SQLMAXMEMORY switches.
Enable buffer pool extensions in SQL Server.
Run the SQL Server setup and specify the /ACTION=REBUILDDATABASE and /SQLCOLLATION switches.

questions.explanation:
Azure Marketplace SQL Server VM images do not use the SQL Server collation required by SAP NetWeaver. The SQL Server system databases must therefore be rebuilt while specifying the required collation by using `/ACTION=REBUILDDATABASE` and `/SQLCOLLATION`.

**Learn more:** [SQL Server Azure Virtual Machines DBMS deployment for SAP NetWeaver](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/dbms-guide-sqlserver)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises network and an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to migrate on-premises SAP workloads to Azure virtual machines. You will use an NFS account in Azure NetApp Files as the storage platform.  
  
You need to ensure that data transferred between the NFS account on the virtual machines and the Azure NetApp Files shares is encrypted.  
  
What should you create first?

options.text: a user-assigned managed identity in the Azure subscription
an Active Directory connection for the NFS account
an Azure key vault in the Azure subscription
a system-assigned managed identity in the NFS account

questions.explanation:
Azure NetApp Files encrypts data in transit for NFSv4.1 by using Kerberos with AES-256. Kerberos ticketing requires an Active Directory Domain Services or Microsoft Entra Domain Services connection; therefore, an Active Directory connection must be created for the Azure NetApp Files account before configuring an NFSv4.1 Kerberos volume.

**Learn more:** [Configure NFSv4.1 Kerberos encryption for Azure NetApp Files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-netapp-files/configure-kerberos-encryption) · [Create and manage Active Directory connections for Azure NetApp Files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-netapp-files/create-active-directory-connections)

You are planning an SAP HANA deployment.  
  
You estimate that the database will reach 1.8 TB within three years.  
  
You must ensure that the deployment supports 60,000 IOPS. The solution must minimize costs while providing the lowest possible latency.  
  
Which disk type should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Ultra Disk is intended for IO-intensive workloads such as SAP HANA. It supports up to 400,000 IOPS per disk and is designed for consistently low sub-millisecond latency. Its capacity, IOPS, and throughput can be provisioned independently, allowing the required 60,000 IOPS to be configured without overprovisioning capacity or performance.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure managed disk types](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/disks-types)

You need to back up the SAP HANA database to vault1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From HANA1, run the SAP HANA backup configuration script.
From HANA1, run the sp_iqrebuildindexforbp SAP HANA command.

questions.explanation:
Azure Backup requires the SAP HANA preregistration (backup configuration) script to be run on the VM hosting SAP HANA before Azure can discover and register the HANA instance with a Recovery Services vault. The script configures the HANA permissions and backup integration needed for protection.\

You have an SAP workload running on an Azure virtual machine.  
  
You have a built-in role-based access control (RBAC) role definition in JSON format.  
  
You plan to convert the built-in role definition into a custom role definition.  
  
Which property value in the built-in role definition must you change?
questions.explanation:
Azure built-in roles have `assignableScopes` set to the root scope (`\"/\"`), which makes them available at all scopes. A custom Azure RBAC role cannot use the root scope; it must specify one or more valid management-group, subscription, or resource-group scopes instead.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understand Azure role definitions - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-definitions) · [Azure custom roles - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/custom-roles)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains a virtual machine named VM1 running SAP HANA, and a user named User1. User1 has the Virtual Machine Contributor role assigned for VM1.  
  
You need to stop User1 from putting VM1 into the **Stopped (deallocated)** state. User1 must still be able to restart the operating system on VM1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a resource lock on VM1.
Assign an Azure Policy definition to the resource group that contains VM1.
Assign User1 the Virtual Machine User Login role for VM1.
Configure the Desired State Configuration (DSC) extension on VM1.

questions.explanation:
A ReadOnly resource lock on the virtual machine overrides RBAC permissions and prevents control-plane modifications, including the POST operation used to deallocate the VM. Restarting the guest operating system from within the VM remains possible because it does not modify the Azure VM resource.

**Learn more:** [Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an SAP environment in Azure.  
  
Your on-premises network connects to Azure through a 1-Gbps ExpressRoute circuit. Private peering is enabled on the circuit, and the on-premises network advertises the default route (`0.0.0.0/0`).  
  
Whenever backups are copied to Azure Blob storage, the ExpressRoute circuit becomes saturated.  
  
You need to resolve the issue without changing the ExpressRoute circuit. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a user-defined route that redirects traffic to the Blob storage
Change the backup solution to use a third-party software that can write to the Blob storage

questions.explanation:
A private endpoint for the Blob service assigns the storage service a private IP address in the virtual network. DNS directs the normal Blob endpoint name to that private IP, and the private endpoint's more-specific interface route takes precedence over the advertised default route. Backup traffic therefore remains on Azure Private Link rather than being sent across the ExpressRoute circuit.

**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-private-endpoints) · [Azure Private Link in a hub-and-spoke network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/networking/guide/private-link-hub-spoke-network)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant called contoso.com.  
  
You are designing an authentication and authorization solution for SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) software-as-a-service (SaaS) applications.  
  
SAP BTP subaccounts trust your company’s SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication Service (IAS) tenant.  
  
You plan to create a trust relationship between the IAS tenant and contoso.com.  
  
You must ensure that authorization decisions in the SAP BTP applications rely exclusively on claims issued by contoso.com.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From IAS, enable the Use Identity Authentication user store option.
From SAP BTP, enable the use of default attributes.
From SAP BTP, disable the use of default attributes.
From IAS, disable the Use Identity Authentication user store option.

questions.explanation:
When IAS is acting as a proxy for a corporate identity provider and **Use Identity Authentication user store** is disabled, IAS sends the application the same attributes that it received from the corporate identity provider. IAS user-store data and default-attribute configuration are not used, so SAP BTP authorization decisions rely only on claims from Microsoft Entra ID (contoso.com).

**Learn more:** [SAP Help Portal — Configure Identity Federation](https://help.sap.com/docs/identity-authentication/identity-authentication/integration-configure-identity-federation) · [SAP Help Portal — Enrich Token Claims Coming from Corporate IdP](https://help.sap.com/docs/identity-authentication/identity-authentication/enrich-token-claims-coming-from-corporate-idp)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An SAP production environment in Azure includes an SAP HANA database.  
  
You need to configure a Recovery Services vault to back up the HANA database server. The solution must allow the virtual machine and the HANA database to be manually restored to a paired region.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a Recovery Services vault in the paired region.
Configure zone-redundant storage (ZRS) replication for the storage.

questions.explanation:
Cross Region Restore enables recovery from replicated recovery points in an Azure paired secondary region and supports both Azure VMs and SAP HANA databases hosted on Azure VMs. It requires a Recovery Services vault configured with geo-redundant storage (GRS); ZRS provides availability-zone redundancy rather than paired-region recovery. A target vault in the secondary region is required when restoring SAP HANA, but enabling CRR is the feature that makes cross-region restore possible.

**Learn more:** [Create and configure Recovery Services vaults - Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-create-recovery-services-vault) · [Restore SAP HANA databases on Azure VMs - Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/sap-hana-database-restore)

You are planning the Azure network infrastructure to meet the disaster recovery requirements.  
  
What is the minimum number of virtual networks needed for the SAP deployment?
questions.explanation:
Cross-region disaster recovery for an SAP workload requires separate virtual networks and subnets in the disaster-recovery region. The primary and disaster-recovery regions therefore require at least one virtual network each, totaling two virtual networks.\

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an SAP production landscape that runs SAP HANA databases on Azure. The HANA database server is a Standard_M32ms Azure virtual machine with 864 GB of RAM.  
  
The HANA database is 400 GB, and you expect it to grow by 40 percent over the next 12 months.  
  
You resize the HANA database server virtual machine to Standard_m64ms with 1,024 GB of RAM.  
  
You need to recommend further changes to minimize performance degradation resulting from database growth.  
  
What should you recommend for the HANA database server?
questions.explanation:
A larger SAP HANA database requires adequately sized data and log storage with sufficient I/O throughput. Adding and correctly configuring disks increases available storage capacity and can provide the required aggregate IOPS and throughput for the growing HANA volumes. The resized VM already supplies the increased compute capacity.

**Learn more:** [SAP HANA Azure virtual machine Premium SSD configurations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/hana-vm-premium-ssd-v1) · [SAP HANA Azure virtual machine storage configurations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/hana-vm-operations-storage)

Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Standard Load Balancer provides load distribution and can support NVA high availability, but it does not by itself steer all Azure-to-on-premises traffic through the appliance. Traffic steering requires user-defined routes that specify the NVA (or an internal load balancer frontend used for the NVA tier) as the next hop.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure virtual network traffic routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-networks-udr-overview) · [Tutorial: Route network traffic with a route table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/tutorial-create-route-table)

Solution: You configure route filters for Microsoft peering.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft-peering route filters select Microsoft service prefixes advertised over an ExpressRoute circuit; they do not steer virtual-network or on-premises traffic through a network virtual appliance. Routing all relevant traffic through the appliance requires user-defined routes with the appliance configured as the next hop.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure route filters for Microsoft peering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/how-to-routefilter-portal) · [Azure ExpressRoute routing requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/expressroute-routing)

Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure user-defined routes can direct traffic from associated subnets to a network virtual appliance by setting it as the next hop. This overrides the default route as needed so traffic is sent through the firewall appliance.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure virtual network traffic routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-networks-udr-overview) · [Tutorial: Route network traffic with a route table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/tutorial-create-route-table)

questions.explanation:
Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS-based load balancer for directing client requests to public-facing endpoints; clients connect directly to the selected endpoint rather than traversing Traffic Manager. It cannot force traffic between Azure subnets and an on-premises network through a network virtual appliance. This requires routing configuration such as user-defined routes with the appliance as the next hop.\
\

questions.explanation:
Azure Site Recovery replicates the OS and data disks attached directly to an Azure VM to a secondary region and supports test failovers for periodic DR testing, but it does not replicate Azure Files shares or Azure NetApp Files volumes, since those are PaaS network-storage endpoints rather than VM-attached disks; Azure Files premium tier additionally has no GRS/cross-region replication option and is not supported for SAP DBMS workloads. Storage Spaces Direct and a Windows Server NFS share, by contrast, run on ordinary Azure VMs with standard managed disks, and Microsoft's Azure Site Recovery support matrix explicitly lists Storage Spaces Direct and Scale-Out File Server configurations as supported for (crash-consistent) Azure-to-Azure replication, satisfying both the Site Recovery and periodic DR-test requirements for the HANA network share.

**Learn more:** [SAP HANA Azure virtual machine storage configurations - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/hana-vm-operations-storage) · [Support matrix for Azure VM disaster recovery with Azure Site Recovery - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/site-recovery/azure-to-azure-support-matrix)

You need to recommend a solution that supports the scale set while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
For SAP workloads, Azure supports and recommends virtual machine scale sets with Flexible orchestration. A scaling profile is not recommended because SAP autoscaling does not work out of the box.\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an SAP NetWeaver deployment on Azure. The SAPMNT share is implemented by using Azure premium file shares.  
  
You plan to implement disaster recovery for the deployment by configuring a secondary site in a paired Azure region.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to replicate the SAPMNT share content to the premium file share in the paired region.  
  
Which two recommendations meet the goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure premium file shares are SSD-based, and Azure Files does not support GRS or GZRS geo-redundancy for SSD file shares. Cross-region replication must therefore be implemented by copying or synchronizing the files between separate shares. Microsoft recommends RoboCopy for SMB Azure Files between sites in SAP disaster-recovery deployments, and supports AzCopy-based scripts for copying Azure Files data to a storage account in a secondary region.

**Learn more:** [Disaster Recovery overview and infrastructure guidelines for SAP workload](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sap/workloads/disaster-recovery-overview-guide) · [Data Redundancy in Azure Files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/files-redundancy)

- Minimize downtime.

options.text: SAP Database Migration Option (DMO) with System Move

questions.explanation:
SAP Database Migration Option (DMO) with System Move is an SAP-supported one-step approach that combines migration of the SAP system to a new target environment with conversion of the database to SAP HANA. Combining these activities reduces the downtime and complexity associated with performing separate moves and database migrations.
